nativePlatform.scope: Library, document preview, and compatible conversation/settings controls. This is not a complete specification of Atlas, Automations, Graph, or Mind Map.
nativePlatform.portableSamples: HTML/CSS samples illustrate content hierarchy and geometry only. Browser system colors and controls do not reproduce NSColor, SwiftUI button styles, SF Symbols, selection, or native focus behavior. Native bindings below and the cited Swift files describe the shipping implementation.

sourceAudit.authority: DESIGN.md and this sidecar were refreshed against the current working-tree SwiftUI implementation, including narrow-preview sizing and observable settings state. Source code supplies implementation facts; DESIGN.md preserves the design direction.
sourceAudit.verification: Source-backed documentation refresh. Narrow-layout and task-observation evidence comes from this session's earlier tests and synthetic offscreen captures, not a new interactive GUI or accessibility audit.

nativeBindings.controlSurface: Color(nsColor: .controlBackgroundColor) for search, composer, and Markdown code blocks
nativeBindings.text: SwiftUI primary/secondary foreground styles; selected or dark sidebar labels explicitly use white, otherwise black
nativeBindings.selection: Native sidebar/inset List selection; appearance and focus remain system-controlled
nativeBindings.accent: DocumentPreview sets tint from the primary category's AtlasPalette ink; native prominent/bordered actions inherit that tint
nativeBindings.separator: SwiftUI Divider; preview hero uses separator strokeBorder at 0.5pt
nativeBindings.icons: SF Symbols; no browser icon substitution is normative

previewActions.adaptation: ViewThatFits switches from text labels to icon-only labels, preserving accessibility labels and help

categoryPalette.source: Gleanary/KnowledgeAtlasRenderer.swift: AtlasPalette; slot chosen by AtlasHierarchy.hue(for:)
categoryPalette.colorSpace: SwiftUI Color(hue:saturation:brightness:); these are HSB values, not CSS HSL

sourceImages.behavior: Locally stored source previews use top-aligned fill and clipping. The detail image is constrained to viewport width. Images repeat the title and are hidden from accessibility. Markdown does not load remote images.

conversationComposer.behavior: Attach, multiline message, Send/Stop/Redirect; no microphone or reasoning selector

nativeBindings.emptyFilingCategories: The map Hide empty preference dims empty sidebar homes consistently in Chat, Automations, and map-mode Library. Chat and Automations load and refresh the shared snapshot even on a cold launch; empty homes remain reachable.
nativeBindings.researchNoteTitles: New Researcher summaries and comparisons receive concise topic-based titles generated from their verified result by the selected provider, then separately evidence-checked before saving. Usually 3–8 words; hard ceilings of 12 words and 80 characters. Two extra bounded model calls. Source names, content, citation links, and existing note titles are unchanged.

conversation.following: Native ScrollPosition follows the bottom within a 40pt tolerance as new messages, streamed text, and layout growth render. User scrolling upward suspends following; returning to the bottom or choosing Latest messages resumes it. Content growth alone does not disable following.
conversation.researchReferences: Separate Summary/Comparison and Source/Sources groups based on persisted artifact/task provenance. Results say Generated by Researcher and omit Research:/Comparison: prefixes only in their displayed titles. Sources retain S1/S2 numbers and an Open website action for HTTP(S) URLs. Chat replaces only the app-added exact source bibliography with these controls, preserving saved Markdown and inline citations.

atlasSourceCards.grouping: One source card includes single-source summaries with the same primary filing home, using persisted provenance. A captured note can anchor the card even when its primary text is a summary, using its retained capture. Multi-source, independently filed, or ambiguous summaries remain separate.
atlasSourceCards.actions: Card metadata shows the summary count, including an anchor note that is itself a summary. Selection exposes Open Source and Open Summary, or a summary menu for multiple summaries; VoiceOver has named source and summary actions. A summarized capture opens its retained original through Open Source, while its primary summary remains a separate menu action.
atlasSourceCards.integrity: Grouping is display-only. Document counts and search include every member; summary navigation resolves to the source card. Notes-only views show summaries independently.

nativeBindings.summaryActions: Library and chat previews share LibraryModel summary availability, the selected provider, progress, cancellation, and automatic preview refresh. Manual generation waits while library work or that source’s page fetch is active.
nativeBindings.adaptiveSummaries: Both providers adapt summary detail to the source, without a point quota: overview only when sufficient, typically 3–6 takeaways for an article, up to 10 with at most 4 neutral section labels for dense material, within a 600-word safety ceiling. Long-source selection retains up to 12 distinct excerpts per section; evidence reviews are bounded by point count and quote volume. Existing summaries are not rewritten.

readingSurface.fill: primary at 0.035 opacity in dark appearance, 0.025 in light
readingSurface.notesPattern: Cached repeating 20pt tile with 1.2pt dots: white at 0.10 opacity in dark appearance, black at 0.08 in light. Clipped to the reading surface; hidden in increased contrast, non-interactive, and hidden from accessibility. Sources remain plain.
readingSurface.typography: Content heading and prose share the Notes/Sources reading font. Provenance, actions, and related items remain outside in system typography.

filingChip.font: .callout; code semibold and monospacedDigit; one-line label
filingChip.fill: AtlasPalette.fill at 0.24 opacity in dark or 0.32 in light for primary homes; 0.08 for secondary
filingChip.border: 1pt AtlasPalette.ink at 0.4 opacity for secondary homes; transparent for primary
filingChip.wrapping: FilingRow uses ChipFlow(spacing: 8), including Suggest/Change actions; each child is measured against available row width. Children share the first text baseline on each row, including padded chips and link buttons; the filing label aligns with the first row.

infoCard.layout: Grid, leadingFirstTextBaseline; 14pt horizontal and 10pt vertical gaps; trailing labels and leading values

settings.appearance: Independent installed font-family and 10–32pt size pickers for Notes and Sources, with live previews and per-group resets. Notes default to Athelas 14pt when installed, otherwise Georgia; Sources to system 14pt. Existing custom choices are preserved. Applies to document reading and editing, not app chrome or chat. Missing fonts fall back to system without clearing the saved choice.
settings.busyBehavior: AI controls are disabled while ConversationModel.running is true. A Stop Task button remains outside the disabled subtree. The running state is observable and clears on worker completion.

title.purpose: Document titles use the selected Notes/Sources family, bold, scaled to 22pt at the default 14pt prose size. Markdown H1 scales to 17pt, semibold; lower headings use the prose size, semibold.

row-title.purpose: LibraryDocumentRow uses body.medium, limited to two lines.

body.purpose: DocumentPreview uses the Notes or Sources font preference: Athelas 14pt when installed (Georgia otherwise) for Notes, system 14pt for Sources. Summaries, comparisons, and Writer documents are Notes. MarkdownPreview defaults to body in chat. Code remains monospaced at the reading size. Paragraph line spacing is 4pt; bullet text uses 3pt.

metadata.purpose: Rows use caption metadata. DocumentPreview source line uses subheadline; its info card and category chips use callout. Counts use monospacedDigit.

nativeLayout.structure: ContentView: manual resizable sidebar beside main content; HSplitView for library list/detail. ConversationView: viewport-aware HSplitView for feed/optional saved-document preview, with composer beneath.

captureList.note: Current shared splitColumns frame applies the same list limits to captures; no separate 360/480 capture-column limits.

conversationPreview.feedMinimum: When shown: min(460, max(240, viewportWidth - 321)); otherwise 240

filingInspector.implementation: Plain trailing column, not SwiftUI inspector

nativeLayout.adaptation: Native split resizing, viewport-constrained reading/image content, ViewThatFits action labels, and wrapping filing chips/actions. No CSS breakpoint scale.

narrative.overview:
Apple design language with ChatGPT-inspired restraint: familiar controls, compact navigation, and a generous reading pane. This records the finished Library and compatible app controls, not a redesign of conversation, settings, Graph, or Mind Map. Deferred graph surfaces keep their existing code and data.

The product's platform posture is adaptive; the shipping surface is SwiftUI on macOS 26+ only. No web, iOS, or Android implementation is implied. Native system typography and SF Symbols are intentional for navigation and controls. Document typography is adjustable in Appearance settings. The only raster images in the Library are locally captured source previews.
keyCharacteristics: Semantic macOS surfaces and system light/dark appearance.
Native sidebar, searchable list, and selectable Markdown reading.
Quiet provenance and explicit handoff to Chat.

rules.name: The Semantic Surface Rule
rules.body: Use native semantic surfaces for Library backgrounds; do not replace them with sampled screenshot colors.

dos: Do preserve native semantic colors, text styles, SF Symbols, and keyboard-accessible controls.
Do distinguish saved sources, generated summaries, and personal notes while keeping originals reachable.
Do keep Library browsing and reading independent of inference.
donts: Don't replace this Library with decorative cards, branded status bars, or a visualization dashboard.
Don't add a second composer or send a request automatically on handoff.
Don't extend these Library decisions into unseen Graph, Mind Map, or settings redesigns.
